name: FinanceToolkit v2.3.4
html:
A release on macro data and on judging how unusual a move is. Producer prices by country come from current official sources, with new export and import price indices; the economic calendar reads as a time series; any series can be ranked against its own history, as a level, a spread or a streak; a stock's market-adjusted move gets its size in money and its rank; a basket's market value compares with a country's GDP. Real interest rates, core CPI and commodity prices since 1960 come by month, a basket of stocks gets its own summed statements, and every MCP answer names the publishers its data comes from. Cached data gives the same answers as fresh data, and the MCP server logs every request again.

Package

All modules

  • Every get_, collect_ and search_ method takes show_columns=, a name or a list of names, e.g. economics.get_shiller_stock_market_data(show_columns=["Price", "CAPE"]). A column level left with a single name is dropped, so the Close of several tickers has the tickers as columns; get_historical_data with one ticker and one column returns a DataFrame (#431).

Economics

  • get_producer_price_index comes from the official publishers without an API key: Eurostat for the euro area, the EU and around 35 European countries, the BLS for the United States (FRED with a key for the full history) and the Bank of Japan's corporate goods price index. The OECD dataset it used stopped in 2022. China has no reachable index and is left out with a note; its monthly year-on-year change is in the economic calendar (#405).
  • get_export_price_index and get_import_price_index from the same publishers (#405).
  • get_economic_calendar(as_series=True) returns each event's actual value (and the consensus estimate) by the period it covers, read from the event text, one column per event (#404).
  • Removed: the model function oecd_model.get_producer_price_index (#405).
  • get_chokepoint_transits: IMF PortWatch's daily ship transits through 28 maritime chokepoints from 2019 (the Strait of Hormuz, Suez, Bab el-Mandeb, Panama, Malacca and more), by ship category, as counts or estimated trade volume in metric tons, summed by week, month, quarter or year (#432).
  • get_commodity_prices: the World Bank Pink Sheet, monthly from 1960 (energy, metals including gold, agriculture, fertilizers), with deflate_with= for prices in today's money (#413).
  • get_consumer_price_index(measure=...) and get_inflation_rate(measure=...): core, energy, food, goods, services and shelter (BLS for the United States, Eurostat HICP aggregates for Europe). The US CPI includes the months the BLS released since the BIS last republished it (#415).
  • get_real_interest_rate is monthly by default (period="yearly" for the annual calculation) and takes rate_type="policy", which covers the euro area (#414).
  • The policy rates add the days since the BIS's weekly update from the Bank of England and the ECB, and get_european_central_bank_rates takes period= (#414).
  • get_government_interest_expenditure (with ratios to GDP and to revenue) and get_government_expenditure_by_function (COFOG, with a ratio to GDP), from the IMF (#407).
  • get_purchasing_power, with overnight_rate=True for the real value of cash; get_consumer_price_index(cumulative=True) and get_overnight_rate(cumulative=True) (#408).
  • Monthly, quarterly and yearly data shows a period a source skipped as an empty row, so a change never compares the wrong periods; annual changes compare the same period a year earlier (#413, #417).
  • The economic calendar series keep a release that covers two months (China's January and February trade) once, under the later month, and leave out releases without a period (#417).
  • Removed: fred_model.get_real_yield_curve and fred_model.get_breakeven_inflation_expectations; the US real yields and breakevens come from the Treasury (#414).

Econometrics

  • get_level_significance: the latest value of any series (a rate, a macro series or a close) with its percentile over the history and the last date it was as high or as low (#402).
  • get_streaks: the current run of positive or negative values of a series, its start and length, the run before it and the longest earlier run of the same sign (#404).
  • spread_over= ranks or counts one series minus another, such as producer minus consumer prices (#404).
  • get_level_significance adds the change since the start, the highest and lowest of the range, the first date above a level=, the annualised change, the largest drawdown with its recovery date, and the rank of the latest value (#409, #410, #413, #416, #417).
  • get_window_change_by_year: the change over the same months every year, ranked (#415).
  • get_streaks(level=...) counts runs above or below a level, and ratio=True divides by the spread_over series instead of subtracting it (#416).
  • With changes="difference", the changes of get_level_significance and get_window_change_by_year are in points, such as the change of a yield over a month (#419).
  • zone=True on the Altman, Zmijewski, Springate and Taffler scores adds the Distress / Grey / Safe zone of each score (#420).
  • get_optimization_backtest shows the return and Sharpe ratio each strategy expected in sample next to what it realised (#420).
  • get_issuer_spreads compares issuers' spreads at the same maturities (2Y, 5Y, 10Y, ...) by interpolating along each issuer's bonds (#420).
  • get_yield_decomposition splits the nominal yield of the United States, United Kingdom and Germany into the real yield and breakeven inflation, with the daily change of each part (#422).
  • Econometrics.get_move_significance measures how unusual each change of any series is, e.g. the largest one-day rise of a yield since a date (#422).
  • get_initial_jobless_claims without a FRED key retries when the Department of Labor's report cannot reach its database, which happens for up to half of the requests, and otherwise serves the cached claims instead of failing (#434).
  • The yearly consumer price index and inflation rate warn about years the Global Macro Database repeats from the year before (inflation 0 by construction, e.g. Germany 1913-1914) and about hyperinflations, after which the yearly average still rises sharply (Germany 1924: +723%) (#435).
  • The per-ticker earnings and dividend calendars keep the scheduled dates after today (the next earnings release); price targets FMP lists under another analyst company than the article names are credited to the named company, and get_price_target_history adds each company's Previous Target, Previous Date and Target Change (#437).
  • The US inflation rate and CPI are the CPI-U for every date range; a range ending before 2025 returned Eurostat's experimental HICP-concept US figures (#422).
  • Returns of currency pairs, cryptocurrencies and low-priced shares from FinancialModelingPrep use an unrounded adjusted close; FMP's is rounded to two decimals (#423).
  • get_millennium_of_macroeconomic_data(deflate_with=...) puts the long-run series in real terms, e.g. the oil price since 1861 in today's dollars (#424).
  • get_weighted_average_cost_of_capital accepts single numbers as well as series (#425, @pengpengyi92).
  • The Merton model leaves a non-positive or non-finite horizon empty instead of solving it (#426, @pengpengyi92).
  • The daily present value of growth opportunities keeps figures dated on non-trading days (#427, @pengpengyi92).
  • The estimated EPS growth rate is empty for invalid single inputs, such as a zero trailing EPS (#428, @pengpengyi92).
  • As-of lookups of the credit models sort histories that are not in date order (#429, @pengpengyi92).

Performance

  • get_beta_implied_return adds the Residual Value (the residual times the market cap at the previous close), the Residual Percentile and the Residual Largest Since date, so one row judges the latest stock-specific move against its history (#401).

Bonds and rates

  • get_taylor_price_change(from_date=...) gives each Treasury's own yield change between two dates, the duration and convexity estimate and the realised price change from the FedInvest prices (#402).
  • get_treasury_rates takes maturities= (#402).
  • get_loan_payment, get_affordable_loan and get_amortization_schedule at the 30-year mortgage rate, or any rate (#409).

Data

  • Futures tickers (BZ=F, CL=F, NG=F and others) return quotes and intraday data, and TTF=F its daily history again (#410).
  • Cached financial statements keep every period that overlaps the requested range, the same as a fresh request. Before, a warm cache could drop the year before the start date that the statements are fetched with, so factor analyses and other measures that need that year could differ between a first and a later call (#398).

Discovery

  • With primary_only=True, the earnings calendar chooses primary listings from the releases of a week either side of the range. A company that reported just before the range, while its listings abroad dated the same release inside it, no longer shows with a listing abroad as its primary one (#398).

Data sources

  • Every data source is checked weekly, FinancialModelingPrep (every endpoint, through the public methods) and FRED included, and a failing source opens an issue (#434).

Documentation

  • Docstrings across the package: Args match the signatures and their defaults, mentions that no API key is needed are gone, and errors are fixed (#433).
  • The example tables of the valuation models, factor analysis and tail dependence are regenerated from the current calculations (#398).
  • The performance and risk docstrings describe their definitions directly (#397).

Ratios

  • Toolkit(tickers, basket=True) adds a company named Total whose statements are the summed statements of the tickers, so its ratios and models weight each company by its size (#412).
  • get_market_cap(share=True) gives each ticker's share of the total market value, and get_market_cap_to_gdp(country=...) divides the total by a country's GDP in US dollars, on each date the previous complete year's (#406, #412).
  • get_net_capital_expenditure: capital expenditure beyond depreciation and amortization (#412).
  • The asset coverage ratio deducts goodwill as well as the other intangible assets (#400). Every tangible measure (asset coverage, return on tangible assets, tangible asset value, price to tangible book) takes the combined goodwill and intangible assets row, or the separate rows where it is missing, with a missing part counting as zero (#403).

Code

  • Log records without a credential keep their arguments, and a credential inside an argument is replaced in that argument, so formatters that read the arguments themselves keep working (#396).
  • soupsieve, used by beautifulsoup4, is locked at 4.1 (2.10 below Python 3.11.5) (#439).
  • opentelemetry-api, used by fastmcp, is locked at 1.45.2 (#440).
  • tornado is locked at 6.6.1 and dnspython at 2.9.2 (#443).

MCP server

  • A series= reference passes period= on to the indicators it reads, and reads a calendar event as a series (#402, #404).

  • Every answer lists the publishers its data comes from under _sources, also when it is answered from the cache or from data loaded by an earlier call (#418).

  • An indicator without a period parameter is converted to the requested period, with a note (#416).

  • Daily prices name the days a ticker did not trade (an exchange holiday), which carry its last close (#419).

  • Instances unused for 30 minutes are dropped and their memory is released, so a long-running server no longer keeps the memory of its busiest moment (#419).

  • rank=true on every tool ranks the tickers or countries within each period, with each one's gap to its neighbour (#421).

  • FT_MCP_COMPACT_TOOLS=1 lists the tools without their long descriptions, and search_metrics with an indicator's name returns its description and parameters (#422).

  • The Altman, Zmijewski, Springate and Taffler scores include their zone by default (#420).

  • The access log writes a line for every request again instead of a logging error, with request paths still free of credentials (#396).

name: FinanceToolkit v2.3.3
html:
A release on correctness, robustness and security, with bonds as a new asset class. Each ticker is now measured on its own trading days and calculated on unrounded data, so the Python package and the MCP server give the same figures. Controller methods work without arguments, bond calculators work on real bonds and market curves, the portfolio optimizers gain new objectives, constraints and a walk-forward backtest, and the MCP server, the cache, data retrieval and the release pipeline are hardened.

Package

Defaults from the data

  • Controller methods work without arguments: the valuation models default to each company's cost of equity (CAPM with its country's equity risk premium) or WACC, the dividend CAGR or the reinvestment growth, with the stable growth kept within 0% and 2.5%, all measured without look-ahead. Rates also take a list or a dict per ticker (#359).
  • With trailing set, the beta of the WACC and residual income covers the trailing periods, so quarterly defaults agree with annual ones (#359).
  • Defaults for get_tail_dependence_coefficient and get_covar (against the benchmark), get_style_analysis (Sharpe's asset classes as ETFs), get_commodity_forward_curve (all eight commodities), get_return_excluding (the largest holding), get_strategy_payoff (an at-the-money straddle) and the Discovery news searches (#359).

Bonds and rates

  • get_treasury_securities lists every marketable US Treasury with price, yield and duration from FedInvest, without an API key. get_bond_universe lists about 9,000 US corporate bonds from bond ETF holdings, with the G-Spread over the Treasury par curve (#356).
  • The bond calculators (collect_bond_statistics, get_present_value, get_duration, get_yield_to_maturity, get_z_spread, get_key_rate_duration, get_taylor_price_change) run on real bonds: by default the benchmark Treasuries, or bonds chosen with bonds=, issuer=, etfs= and a maturity range. The rate calculators read a country's government bond curves on a day (#358).
  • get_implied_default_probability takes ratings= and uses the latest ICE BofA spread per rating (#358).
  • Removed: get_option_adjusted_spread, get_derivative_price and the parameters for typing in a bond's terms by hand (#358).

Economic data without a FRED key

  • Initial jobless claims, retail sales, housing starts, real personal income, nonfarm payrolls and the HQM corporate bond curve and spread come straight from the Department of Labor, Census Bureau, BEA, BLS and Treasury when no FRED key is set, identical to FRED over their full history (#357).

Portfolio optimization

  • get_maximum_diversification_weights, get_minimum_tracking_error_weights (with objective="information_ratio") and get_growth_optimal_weights (Kelly, with fraction=), and covariance="denoised" (López de Prado) in every optimizer and in get_risk_contributions, (#362).
  • Per-asset weight bounds (one number or a dict per ticker), sector_bounds= and country_bounds= from the company profiles, and net_exposure and gross_exposure for long-short portfolios in every optimizer; risk parity takes weight, sector and country bounds (constrained risk budgeting) and HRP weight bounds. Infeasible constraints are refused with the reason (#378).
  • get_hierarchical_equal_risk_contribution_weights (HERC, Raffinot), get_nested_clustered_optimization_weights (NCO, López de Prado), get_minimum_drawdown_weights (CDaR, maximum or average drawdown), get_maximum_omega_weights and get_maximum_cvar_ratio_weights (#385, merged through #386).
  • get_optimization_backtest: a walk-forward backtest that re-optimizes on each monthly, quarterly or yearly date from the trailing returns, without look-ahead, against equal weights and the benchmark, with turnover and transaction costs (#386, #391).
  • current_weights= with maximum_turnover= and transaction_cost= in the optimizers, and expected_returns= ('mean', 'exponential', 'capm' or Jorion's 'james_stein') (#386, #391).
  • get_resampled_efficient_weights (Michaud resampling), get_diversification_metrics (concentration, effective number of assets and of bets, diversification ratio) and get_risk_contributions(risk_measure="cvar") for the contributions to expected shortfall. Every CVaR uses the exact Rockafellar-Uryasev tail (#386, #391).
  • covariance= gains the Ledoit-Wolf constant-correlation and single-factor targets, codependence= ('pearson', 'spearman' or 'kendall') sets the correlation behind HRP, HERC and NCO, get_mean_variance_weights takes target_volatility= for the highest expected return at a volatility, and Black-Litterman takes risk_aversion="market" (implied by the benchmark) and reports the posterior volatility (#394).
  • get_discrete_allocation turns weights into whole shares for a portfolio value (integer programme or greedy), get_portfolio_risk_metrics gives the return, volatility, Sharpe, Sortino, maximum drawdown, VaR and CVaR of given weights next to the benchmark, and get_risk_contributions adds semideviation, mean absolute deviation and CDaR (#393).
  • The portfolio docstrings describe every optimizer by its paper and formula (#392).
  • Removed: optimization_model.get_black_litterman_returns returning only the returns; it now returns the returns and the posterior covariance (#394).

Ratios

  • Gross profitability (Novy-Marx), operating profitability (Fama-French), cash-based operating profitability, cash return on invested capital, free cash flow conversion, free cash flow to EBITDA, capex intensity and capex to depreciation (#361).
  • EBITDA, EBITDA minus capex and cash interest coverage, FFO to debt and discretionary cash flow to debt (S&P, Moody's), the degrees of operating, financial and total leverage, the free cash flow payout ratio, EV to invested capital and price to tangible book (#373).
  • The investment and issuance anomalies: asset growth (Cooper, Gulen and Schill), net operating assets (Hirshleifer et al.), percent accruals (Hafzalla, Lundholm and Van Winkle), net share issuance (Pontiff and Woodgate), composite equity issuance (Daniel and Titman) and net external financing (Bradshaw, Richardson and Sloan) (#380).

Models

  • get_altman_z_score(model=...): the original Z, Z' (private firms), Z'' (non-manufacturers) and Z''-EM (emerging markets), each with Altman's own coefficients and zones, and get_taffler_z_score, the UK model of Taffler (1983) (#369).
  • get_campbell_hilscher_szilagyi_score: the failure probability of Campbell, Hilscher and Szilagyi (2008), with its components (#390).
  • On quarterly data the distress scores (Altman, Taffler, Ohlson, Zmijewski, Springate, Grover, Fulmer, Piotroski, Beneish) cover a trailing year and compare with the same quarter a year earlier (#387).
  • The valuation models warn when the required return is less than two percentage points above the growth kept forever (#387).
  • Removed: the model function parameter market_value_of_equity_to_book_value_of_total_liabilities_ratio of altman_model.get_altman_z_score, now equity_to_total_liabilities_ratio (#369).

Risk and performance

  • Each ticker uses its own trading days, and measures against the benchmark pair returns only on dates both traded (#353).
  • The drawdown table gains calendar-day and year durations, and get_drawdown_series a deepest_since= date (#354).
  • Calculations run on unrounded prices, returns and Treasury yields; only the returned tables are rounded (#367).
  • Lo's autocorrelation-adjusted Sharpe ratio (method="lo", with Moran's bias correction and at least 30 returns), get_sharpe_ratio_standard_error (iid, non-normal and GMM), get_minimum_track_record_length, and get_coskewness and get_cokurtosis with the benchmark (#379).
  • Drawdown and tail ratios no longer drop a period for every ticker when one ticker has no value; a zero denominator gives NaN instead of ±inf; returns that do not vary have no skewness or kurtosis; and a bad OHLC bar only leaves out that day in the range-based volatility estimators (#364).

Robustness

  • Supplied historical= data is checked and normalised (dates of any type, sorted, duplicates removed, returns calculated when missing), and supplied statements without a ticker level or with repeated line items are refused with a clear message (#371).
  • All Options methods carry @handle_errors; a ticker without a price on the pricing date is left out instead of failing the others, and a start_date on a non-trading day uses the last trading day before it (#371).
  • The package no longer silences RuntimeWarnings for the whole process (#371).
  • Symbols are percent-encoded in every FMP request, so M&M.NS is no longer read as Macy's (M); FMP errors sent with status 200 are classified, and one failing ticker no longer discards the results of the others (#363).

Analyst estimates

  • The latest price target's date and the days since it (#355).
  • The number of analysts behind the revenue and the EPS estimates as separate rows, and min_analysts= on the forward P/E and PEG to leave out thinly covered years. Estimate years follow the same calendar labelling as the statements, so for fiscal years ending January to May they move one year back and the forward PEG compares the right years. Removed: the averaged "Number of Analysts" row (#381).
  • The market-wide earnings calendar returns every release of a range instead of the latest 4,000, with each company's name, exchange and market cap in USD (from its primary listing), and min_market_cap, country, exchange, primary_only and sort_by (#381).

Commodities

  • get_commodity_term_structure: the front and far contracts, spread, slope, annualised roll yield and backwardation or contango per date, on the curve as listed each day or on fixed contracts (#382).
  • get_commodity_forward_curve takes generic=True for the front month and the next eleven as listed each day, and growth/lag; its end date is now included (#382).

Technicals

  • One get_moving_average(method=...) for the simple, exponential, double exponential, triangular, weighted and Hull moving averages. Removed: get_exponential_moving_average, get_double_exponential_moving_average, get_triangular_moving_average, get_weighted_moving_average and get_hull_moving_average (#388).
  • signals_only=True on get_signals and get_candlestick_patterns keeps only the days with a signal or pattern (#352).

Data sources

  • Fiscal periods are labelled alike from FMP and Yahoo Finance: a period ending in the first five days of a month counts as ending in the month before, which keeps the quarters of 52/53-week years that were dropped before. Yahoo statistics carry the fiscal quarter, so its filing deadlines match. Removed: yfinance_model.get_reported_currency, now get_company_information (#389).
  • Results whose periods have a multiplier, such as 2M, keep their period (#383).
  • The cache stores data as compressed JSON instead of pickle, so reading a cache file never runs code (#366).

Security

  • Only the FMP and FRED keys are read from .env files, never over a key already set in the environment; API keys are removed from every log message and traceback; the setup wizard writes its files readable only by you (#368).

Economics

  • Removed: get_real_gross_domestic_product_usd, the same series as get_gross_domestic_product(inflation_adjusted=True, usd=True) (#388).

Code

  • Misspelt names corrected, without aliases: get_gordon_growth_model (was get_gorden_growth_model), show_ticker_separation (was show_ticker_seperation), oecd_model.get_trust_in_government and the stock_simulation_dictionary parameter; duplicated value splitting and API key checks merged; unused pylint comments removed (#384).
  • Duplicated helpers merged into one place and dead code removed, including the unused constants Toolkit.TICKER_LIMIT and historical_model.TREASURY_LIMIT, portfolio.helpers.Style and SQLiteBackend.read_series and read_coverage (#374).
  • Docstring fixes across the package (#352).

MCP server

  • risk_free_rate ('13w', '5y', '10y' or '30y'; default '10y') on the performance, risk, models and portfolio tools (#367).
  • The earnings calendar answers with primary listings ranked by market cap by default (#381).
  • Size limits per call on simulations, backtests (lookback at most 504 days), resamples, strike grids, downloads and repeated fits, a 180-second time limit and at most three running calls per user when hosted, and responses cut to size before they are built (#360).
  • MCP_HOST defaults to 127.0.0.1 with DNS rebinding protection on loopback; forwarded headers are trusted only from FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS; tickers are validated before they reach a URL; a hosted server never retries without TLS verification (#360).
  • Sign-in tokens are encrypted and last 24 hours, renewed by 90-day refresh tokens; registered clients are bound to their redirect addresses; pending authorization codes are limited per client address (#360, #368).
  • The Docker image pins its base image by digest, installs dependencies at build time and runs as a non-root user (#365).

Release pipeline

  • Merging a release PR publishes it to PyPI, GitHub and the MCP Registry after an approval, GitHub Actions are pinned to commit SHAs, and Dependabot keeps those pins and the Docker base image current (#365, #376, #377).
  • Offline tests block the network, and the calculations that no test covered are tested against values worked out by hand (#370, #375).

name: FinanceToolkit v2.3.2
html:
A large release with new analytics throughout the package: factor analysis (predictive power) in every module, return decomposition, earnings surprises, ETF contributions, alternative betas, Morningstar's risk-adjusted return, drawdown tables, candlestick patterns and indicator summaries. New data comes from analyst targets, 13F ownership, FINRA short volume, historical index constituents, the NY Fed, the BIS and Damodaran. The MCP setup wizard now writes to the right places for Claude Desktop on Linux, Devin Desktop and VS Code.

Package

New analytics

  • Factor analysis (predictive power): get_factor_analysis in ratios, technicals, models, risk and performance tests any metric, a list of them or a collection (e.g. ratios="valuation") as a cross-sectional signal: information coefficient (mean, IR, t-stat), quantile returns, top-minus-bottom spread, turnover and rank autocorrelation, without look-ahead. performance.get_factor_analysis also takes your own signal as a DataFrame (#335).
  • Returns explained: models.get_return_decomposition splits a price return into EPS growth × P/E change, plus dividends (#320). performance.get_beta_implied_return gives the beta-implied return, the actual return and the residual per period (#344). risk.get_move_significance shows how unusual a move is: volatility multiple, percentile and "largest since" date (#324).
  • Earnings: get_earnings_surprise gives EPS and revenue surprises, SUE, and the share's reaction against the benchmark per announcement (#321).
  • ETFs: etf.get_contribution gives each holding's or sector's contribution to the return (also in index points), and etf.get_return_excluding the return without chosen holdings or sectors (#322). etf.get_active_share (#339).
  • Performance: alternative betas via get_beta(method=...): Blume, Vasicek, Dimson, Scholes-Williams, upside and downside (#325). get_kelly_criterion and get_return_statistics (profit factor, payoff ratio, expectancy, streaks, recovery factor) (#336). Morningstar Risk-Adjusted Return and Morningstar Risk, checked against Morningstar's April 2023 methodology (#339).
  • Risk: get_drawdown_series and get_drawdown_table (#323), with the gain needed to recover: get_drawdown_series(recovery=True) and a Recovery Needed column (#350). get_move_significance also gives the VaR Multiple, a move divided by its trailing VaR (#350).
  • Portfolio: covariance= on every optimiser: sample, Ledoit-Wolf, OAS, semicovariance or exponential. Matches scikit-learn and PyPortfolioOpt (#326).
  • Models: H-model, three-stage DDM (transition_periods=), justified P/E and P/B, and get_intrinsic_valuation(historical=True) (#341). get_quality_score, a Quality Minus Junk composite (#343).
  • Growth: compound=True with growth=True, lag=n gives the n-period CAGR of statements, estimates and every ratio (#329).
  • Technicals: get_candlestick_patterns, 15 patterns identical to TA-Lib, and get_signals (crossovers, RSI zones, band breaks, new highs/lows) (#338). get_indicator_summary gives an indicator's latest value, its percentile and rank in its own history, its extremes with dates, threshold crossings and the average returns after them (#348).

New data

  • Analyst price targets, target history and monthly recommendations (#328). Institutional ownership from 13F filings (#333). FINRA daily short sale volume (#337).
  • Index constituents on a past date, plus the dated changes (#330).
  • NY Fed ACM Treasury term premium and Global Supply Chain Pressure Index (#331). BIS credit-to-GDP gap, debt service ratios and credit to GDP by sector (#332). Damodaran industry averages (#334).

Fixes

  • A ticker without data no longer adds calendar days to the other tickers (#318).
  • Yahoo Finance prices are taken unrepaired when yfinance's repair extra (scikit-learn) is missing, instead of failing (#327).
  • A daily bar fetched before its session closed is asked for again after the close (#345).
  • Technical indicators are calculated on a year of prices before the start date, so smoothed indicators (RSI, ATR, ADX, MACD, moving averages) no longer depend on it (#349).
  • The daily P/E, P/B, earnings yield and dividend yield carry the latest reported figures to the latest close instead of dropping periods before the start date (#349).
  • get_factor_analysis leaves out a metric that fewer than three tickers have (e.g. the preferred dividend coverage ratio in ratios.get_factor_analysis(metrics="all")), with a warning, instead of failing the whole analysis.

MCP server

  • limit selects rows per ticker in multi-ticker answers (#342).
  • A requested ticker that is also the benchmark is returned by methods without a benchmark, such as quotes (#346).
  • benchmark_ticker "None", "null" or "" means no benchmark (#318).
  • All new methods are available on their tools; there are still 25 router tools.
  • A note says when the last daily row comes from an unclosed session (#345).
  • Setup wizard (financetoolkit-mcp-setup):
    • Claude Desktop's Linux path is ~/.config/Claude.
    • The Windsurf client is replaced by "Devin Desktop (Windsurf)" (devin): it writes ~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json, or the old Windsurf file where it still exists.
    • VS Code entries carry "type": "stdio".
    • A new copilot client writes the global ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json.
  • server.json is published to the MCP Registry on every release (#319), and financetoolkit.mcpb is built and attached to every release by the release workflow (#351).

Removed

  • The windsurf choice of financetoolkit-mcp-setup --client; use devin.

The version is 2.3.2 in pyproject.toml, server.json, the bundle manifest, mcp_server/mcpb/pyproject.toml (including the financetoolkit[mcp]== pin) and uv.lock.

name: FinanceToolkit v2.3.1
html:
Some minor new functionalities that resolve edge cases and potential security flaws. Also introduced point-in-time mode as suggested by #298.

Package

New

  • Point-in-time mode (Toolkit(..., point_in_time=True), #301, closes #298).
    • Statements, ratios and models use each period's figures only from the day they were filed (FMP's accepted and filing dates, otherwise the reporting deadline).
    • end_date works as an "as of" date.
    • The statistics statement now holds the Filing Date and Fiscal Year.
  • Country equity risk premium in the Cost of Equity (#307).
    • CAPM, WACC, EVA, residual income and PVGO use the Damodaran premium of each company's country instead of the benchmark's historical excess return.
    • An explicit market_risk_premium still wins.
    • AAPL's 2024 WACC goes from 0.1947 to 0.0823.
  • Portfolio performance on the MCP server. The new tool portfolio_performance takes a portfolio as transactions, holdings, weights or a preset. It returns the overview, performance, positions, transactions and the money-weighted return.

Improved

  • Toolkit core (#300, #305):
    • Quarterly data looks back far enough for the trailing year and its growth in the first periods.
    • Supplied statements are never downloaded again and detect their own date order.
    • Statement periods after end_date are left out.
    • Exchange rates older than a month aren't used.
    • Inputs are validated (tickers, benchmark, lag, dates).
  • Data layer (#304):
    • The price cache refetches when a dividend or split rescales the adjusted history.
    • Prices with a failed dividend or adjusted-close request aren't cached.
    • API keys are removed from logged errors.
    • Discovery queries are URL-encoded ("AT&T", "Aerospace & Defense").
    • Certificate errors fail at once instead of retrying for minutes.
    • On the Free plan, dividends before the latest five come from Yahoo Finance.
  • Portfolio (#311):
    • Transactions in several currencies are converted to one reporting currency at each day's rate; pence and pounds are unified.
    • Purchases come before sales within a day.
    • Decimal commas are read per column.
    • The stored data is not rounded.
  • Utilities and cache (#311):
    • Growth is NaN around a gap.
    • standardize covers the shown window.
    • Cache entries are evicted daily, and the coverage of a cached range never extends past today.
  • Heavy calculations are bounded (#306): option, bond, Monte Carlo and binomial models cap their sizes.
  • Edge-case fixes:
    • Brinson, Black-Litterman, cointegration, YTM, DCC-GARCH, Omega and the MWR (#306).
    • SAR, OBV, the McClellan Oscillator, Supertrend, support/resistance and the volume indicators per ticker over gaps (#309).
    • ETFs compared on common dates (#299).
    • Hurst lags (#297).
    • Brinson looks through funds (#296).
  • Speed (#310): the rolling CVaR, CDaR and Omega, the grouped Ulcer Index and period resampling are vectorised.
  • Clearer messages (#308): a missing key outside the statements says which data is missing, and inflation expectations name the countries they cover.
  • Fixes in this PR:
    • Discovery:
      • The screener sends the upper market cap bound.
      • UK home listings are recognised (SHEL.L instead of the NYSE ADR).
    • Performance: the whole-period Omega, Gain-to-Pain and Rachev ratios are no longer empty.
    • Company data:
      • Annual ESG scores take the year's latest disclosure.
      • Missing revenue segments are NaN, and names keep FMP's spelling ("iPhone").
      • A changed actual_dates applies to a cached earnings calendar.
      • Statements and analyst estimates are stored unrounded, so the rounding of a first call no longer sticks.
      • The statistics statement follows start_date and end_date.
    • Docstrings: the WLS and GLS examples use the estimated weights and the AR(1) Omega.
  • Docs and packaging (#302): docstring defaults match the code, and the package metadata has project links.

Breaking

  • The reverse_dates and smooth_widow parameters are removed (#305, #302).
  • ROC, PPO, TRIX and the KST are decimals instead of percentages (#309).
  • Economics country names follow the Global Macro Database: Macedonia, Macau, Cape Verde, Sao Tome and Principe. The official names are accepted too (#309).
  • The rolling Omega is inf for a window with gains and no losses, like get_omega_ratio (#306, #310).

MCP server

  • Tools:
    • New tool portfolio_performance. Its inputs are validated before anything is fetched (one way to describe the portfolio, at most 1,000 transactions and 50 tickers), and transactions never reach the server as a file path.
    • 25 router tools.
  • OAuth hardening (#303):
    • Single-use authorization codes that expire after 5 minutes.
    • Validated redirect URIs.
    • PKCE S256 is required.
    • Field length caps.
    • An invalid token gets a 401.
  • Request handling (#303):
    • Tools run in a bounded thread pool with a lock per cached Toolkit.
    • A call waiting for a busy Toolkit gives up its slot.
    • Default dates are computed per call.
    • Ticker, search and series counts are capped.
    • Credentials are redacted from the access log.
    • The secret file is created private.
  • Inputs (#295): fractional, JSON and estimated inputs are accepted.

Other

  • Tests:
    • The flaky CI tests are fixed. 16 portfolio and point-in-time tests built Toolkits from supplied prices but without Treasury data, so valuing them retrieved Treasury yields from Yahoo Finance in parallel threads, which locked yfinance's SQLite cache ("database is locked"). Every such Toolkit now gets the supplied Treasury yields; with yfinance blocked, no test reaches it any more. Another test re-read the shared Portfolio's dataset and sent later tests online; it now uses its own Portfolio, and each test process gets its own yfinance cache.
    • 20 technical indicator tests that only recorded NaN now run on 60 sample bars and assert values.
    • New offline tests for the company data parsers.
  • Weekly source checks: a source that returns nothing is reported with what it logged, and a refusal over a request limit is skipped. The BLS allows 25 keyless requests a day per IP address, which GitHub's runners share (#315).
  • Dependencies:
    • tabulate moves from the mcp extra to the dev group.
    • Dependabot: tornado 6.6, joserfc 1.7.6, authlib 1.9.1, dnspython 2.9.0 (#312–#314, #316).
  • Dead code: the dead "pip install yfinance" branches are removed (yfinance is a required dependency).

name: FinanceToolkit v2.3.0
html:
New release with some new modules, lots of verification checks and overall improvements. See the complete list below.

Library

New

  • toolkit.portfolio: optimal weights (minimum variance, maximum Sharpe, mean-variance, risk parity, HRP, inverse volatility, minimum CVaR, Black-Litterman), efficient frontier, risk contributions, stress tests, look-through exposure and Brinson-Fachler attribution. Portfolio takes weights, holdings or transactions and ships 13 presets (#281).
  • toolkit.etf: holdings, weightings, profile with premium/discount to NAV (stale_nav=True for a NAV that is not current), tracking, concentration, overlap, look-through valuation and liquidity (#288).
  • Models: peer comparison, Merton distance to default, synthetic credit rating, reverse DCF, Monte Carlo valuation and more (#282).
  • Options: put/call ratio, max pain, gamma exposure, implied move, model-free implied volatility and the volatility risk premium (#283).
  • Fixed income: zero-coupon curves, Nelson-Siegel-Svensson, yield curve PCA, Vasicek/CIR/Hull-White, callable bond OAS, implied default probabilities and Treasury auctions (#284).
  • Econometrics on any series (Econometrics(data=...)), Markov regime switching, structural breaks, time-varying beta, DCC-GARCH and pairs trading (#285).
  • Performance and technicals: style analysis, regional Fama-French factors, market breadth, seasonality, relative strength and index constituents (#287).

Improved

  • Modules load statements and prices only when a calculation needs them (#290).
  • Every calculating method documents its formula with the defaults it uses, and every docstring example is regenerated live (#286).
  • Correctness, verified against the sources (#286): decimals everywhere, the traded close for market values, no look-ahead (figures apply from the fiscal period end), each ticker keeps its own history, quarterly ratios over a trailing year, continuous rates for options, the arch backcast for GARCH, and many method-level fixes.
  • show_columns selects numeric column labels such as years, thanks to @jackiectl2 (#292).

Breaking

  • Toolkit.get_etf_holdings, get_etf_information, get_etf_sector_weightings and get_etf_country_weightings moved to toolkit.etf (get_holdings and so on).
  • ICE BofA option-adjusted spreads and the discovery quote changes are decimals.
  • A Toolkit whose only ticker is the benchmark raises a clear error; pass benchmark_ticker=None.

MCP server

  • New portfolio and etf tools: 24 router tools.
  • Econometrics takes series= to analyse any indicator.
  • Descriptions follow the new methods, units and defaults; the bundle manifest is synced.

Other

  • A weekly GitHub Actions run checks every keyless data source and opens an issue per broken source (#289).

name: FinanceToolkit v2.2.3
html:
Mostly work for the MCP server to provide more reliable answers.

MCP server

  • Answers stay readable: anything over 60,000 characters is cut to the most recent rows, with a note on how to narrow it. limit works as head/tail (5 first, -5 last) on every tool. Large outputs (simulations, binomial tree, ETF holdings) have compact defaults.
  • Better discovery: search_metrics returns the exact indicator and its tool and understands analyst wording ("how expensive is the stock"). The server sends usage instructions on connect. Every parameter has a real description, from the docstrings.
  • Notes explain the answer: tickers without data, ignored arguments, yearly-only data, sample yield curves, assumed bond inputs, where a series ends, fiscal-year mapping and currency conversion.
  • Inputs: show_columns matches any casing and countries accept short forms (USA, UK). Weights, yield curves, option strategy legs and lists can be passed. Transcripts come back in full per company and fiscal period. Option chains say which expiry they show.
  • Hosted server: at most 4 Economics and 64 Toolkit instances are kept, and one Global Macro Database copy is shared per process (memory stays flat across date ranges).
  • Tools: search_instruments is removed (Finance Database covers it), search_categories is renamed search_metric_categories, and EGARCH is no longer offered (~45s per fit).

Package

  • Stale FMP data fixed: Commitment of Traders, sector and industry history and 8-K filings now request a date range.
  • Stock screener: market caps are in USD, primary_only keeps the home listing, and it returns stocks only unless is_etf=True.
  • Symbols: ISIN/CUSIP/CIK search uses its own parameters, and currency and crypto pairs are accepted in either notation (EURUSD or EURUSD=X).
  • Economics: quarterly and monthly rates use sources with that frequency, calendar event matching ignores spaces and hyphens, and Current Policies climate scenarios work.
  • Fixes and additions:
    • Daily GARCH forecasts are dated by business day.
    • Gainers and losers are sorted by change and ETF weights largest first.
    • Gross margin is empty where cost of goods sold is zero.
    • The Sharpe ratio takes annualize.
    • Option chains take strike_price_range.

name: FinanceToolkit v2.2.2
html:
This release adds new FMP endpoints and recent economic and market data from official sources that need no API key. It also adds scenario and credit inputs, caches external data by default, speeds up many calculations, and fixes a range of calculations and data issues.

New data

  • FinancialModelingPrep:
    • Toolkit: executives and compensation, company notes, employee count, shares float, M&A, stock splits, insider statistics, stock grades, ETF holdings, information and weightings, and earnings call transcripts. Stock news now covers crypto and forex.
    • Discovery: market-wide earnings calendar, 8-K filings and latest insider trades.
    • Economics: economic calendar and market risk premium (optional key).
  • No API key needed:
    • Monthly inflation, CPI and unemployment; quarterly GDP growth.
    • Daily policy, overnight and long-term rates.
    • Government yield curves for nine economies, plus every EU member's 10-year yield.
  • FRED no longer required for the mortgage rate, industrial production, the recession indicator, real yields and breakevens. FRED is still used when a key is set.
  • Credit:
    • The Treasury's HQM corporate curve and spreads, and Moody's Aaa/Baa yields.
    • The excess bond premium and corporate bond yields by country.
    • Rating transition matrices and default rates from ESMA's CEREP database.
    • ECB borrowing costs and stress index.
  • Insurance and long horizons:
    • EIOPA risk-free curves, incl. shocks and the symmetric adjustment.
    • Eurostat life tables and Shiller's US stock market data.
    • Long-run asset returns 1870–2020 (opt-in, non-commercial licence).
    • The Bank of England's UK series from 1086.
  • Scenario inputs:
    • Real and breakeven inflation curves for the US, UK and Germany, and survey inflation expectations.
    • Implied volatility indices (VIX, VSTOXX, MOVE).
    • Fed and ESRB stress-test scenarios and DNB pension scenario sets.
    • NGFS climate scenarios and the EU carbon price.
    • Listed proxies for private markets.
  • Global Macro Database: uses the latest quarterly release. IMF projections are excluded by default.

Caching

  • On by default: data from external sources is cached in the Toolkit, Economics, Fixed Income, Discovery and Portfolio modules. Each dataset is refreshed on its own schedule, and calculated metrics are never cached.
  • Empty answers: an answer that a source has no data is cached too; a failed request is not.
  • FMP first: with an FMP key, FMP data takes priority. Yahoo Finance is used when it has the longer history, for example on the Free plan.

Performance

Before After
EGARCH / GARCH 186 s / 7.9 s 13 s / 1.2 s
Monte Carlo option prices 66 s 2.5 s
All option greeks 5.4 s 0.15 s
All technical indicators 3.3 s 0.7 s
from financetoolkit import Toolkit 2.5 s 0.9 s
Reading prices from the cache 3.8 s 1.1 s

Excel files are read with calamine, modules load on first use, and repeated module access is about twice as fast.

Breaking changes

  • get_real_yield_curve and get_breakeven_inflation_expectations take countries= and return (Country, Maturity) columns labelled 5Y.
  • The market risk premium and percentage releases in the economic calendar are now decimals.
  • GMDB series end at the last observation; gmdb_forecasts=True on a method includes the projections.
  • Corrected calculations change some results:
    • Drawdowns now count a loss on the first day.
    • RSI and CMO start one day later, matching Wilder's definition and TA-Lib.
    • Growth from zero is missing instead of infinite.
    • Missing values no longer skew beta, VaR/CVaR or the portfolio average.
  • External data is cached by default. Opt out with use_cached_data=False or FINANCE_TOOLKIT_CACHE_ENABLED=0.
  • Requests carrying an API key are no longer retried without certificate verification. Behind a corporate proxy, set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE; the README Q&A explains how.

Fixes

  • Data:
    • FMP timeouts and server errors are retried per ticker instead of failing the whole request.
    • Cached prices survive a provider switch.
    • Holidays no longer invent returns or volume.
    • CIK and CUSIP keep their leading zeros.
    • Yahoo listing dates use the exchange's timezone.
  • Calculations:
    • WACC is correct for companies without debt, and the Graham Number for loss-making companies.
    • Barrier options are priced correctly once the barrier has been crossed.
    • Black-Scholes at expiry, bond coupon counts and yields, and binomial tree inputs are handled correctly.
  • Consistency:
    • rounding=0 and rounding=None work everywhere.
    • One error handler serves all modules, so strict mode now covers Performance and Technicals.
  • Other:
    • EIOPA shocked curves and the life tables are fixed.
    • The enterprise value breakdown and implied volatility work again.
    • The economic calendar's order is now deterministic.
    • Moved BIS, Fed and NBER endpoints are updated.
  • Docstrings: all 553 examples were run and their output tables refreshed.

MCP server

  • New methods are added to the existing tools, and an empty result explains why.
  • Tool descriptions are no longer cut off.
  • Daily rolling performance metrics work.
  • A hosted server caches every source except FMP.
  • Optional usage statistics at /stats with FT_MCP_ANALYTICS=1.
  • The server reports the Finance Toolkit's version to clients.

Dependencies

All new requirements use wide version ranges, so the Finance Toolkit fits alongside other packages without forcing upgrades.

Change Package Why
Added python-calamine>=0.3.0 Reads Excel workbooks up to 10× faster than openpyxl. Used for the large official workbooks, such as the Bank of England, EIOPA and ESRB files. Not installed on Python 3.15 until wheels are published there; openpyxl reads the files instead.
Added xlrd>=2.0 Reads the older .xls workbooks some official sources still publish, when calamine is not available or cannot read a file.
Declared numpy>=1.26, scipy>=1.10 Already used throughout, but until now they were only installed because other packages depended on them. They are now listed explicitly.
Removed scikit-learn Only used for the linear regressions of the factor models (e.g. Fama-French). These now use SciPy's least squares, with the same results, which removes a large dependency.

Unchanged: pandas>=3.0, requests, yfinance, openpyxl and pyyaml, and the optional econometrics and mcp extras.

name: FinanceToolkit v2.2.1
html:
A focused maintenance release. Its most urgent fix: a fresh install of the 2.2.0 MCP server crashed on startup, because the mcp dependency had no upper bound and mcp 2.x removed a module the server imports. The local install command on the website therefore failed for everyone. This release caps mcp below 2.0 and fixes two MCP data bugs on top: the rates tool returned no Treasury yields at all, and a benchmark that was also a requested ticker was silently swapped for a different index.

The second theme is daily-first analysis. Risk and Econometrics now default to daily calculations over the whole series instead of quarterly/yearly per-period values, which removes the intraday-data requirement that made period="daily" unusable in Econometrics. Some results change for existing code as a result; see Changed Defaults below.

Underneath, data collection is faster and better behaved. A bounded worker pool replaces one thread per ticker, HTTP connections are reused, and retries back off with jitter. The package now ships type information (py.typed), and the type checker runs in CI.

Every method below hangs off the matching Toolkit sub-module (e.g. toolkit.risk.get_value_at_risk()) or its standalone class (Economics(...), FixedIncome(...), Discovery(...)). Full runnable examples live in the documentation, which now has a dedicated page for every method.

Changed Defaults

  • Econometrics defaults to period="daily" across all methods (previously quarterly or yearly, depending on the Toolkit). within_period now defaults to False on the five diagnostic tests that take it (ARCH-LM, Jarque-Bera, Ljung-Box, CUSUM, Variance Ratio). Every Econometrics method previously rejected period="daily" outright, even though only the within-period nesting needs intraday data. Intraday data is now only required for period="daily" combined with within_period=True, and the error message says how to avoid it. Full examples: docs/econometrics.
  • Risk defaults to period="daily" and within_period=False as well, so metrics such as Value at Risk, CVaR and the GARCH family are calculated over the whole daily series by default. Per-period aggregates (variance, volatility, excess volatility, MAD, coefficient of variation) keep their quarterly/yearly default, since a single daily return has no spread to measure. Full examples: docs/risk.
  • If your code relied on the old defaults, pass period="quarterly"/"yearly" (and within_period=True) explicitly to get the previous behaviour.

Performance

  • Bounded worker pool. Every data collection function used to start one bare thread per ticker, with a 0.1-second stagger between them. A 100-ticker universe spent 10 seconds just starting threads, exceptions died silently inside their thread, and the number of concurrent API calls grew with the universe. All 13 collection sites now share one ThreadPoolExecutor with 10 workers by default (configurable via FINANCETOOLKIT_MAX_WORKERS) that re-raises worker exceptions.
  • Connection reuse. Every request goes through one shared requests session with enlarged connection pools, so repeated calls to the same API reuse TCP connections and TLS handshakes instead of paying for a new handshake each time.
  • Retries back off with jitter, so ten workers hitting a rate limit don't all retry at the same moment.
  • Treasury rate windows are fetched in parallel through the same pool, instead of one by one with sleeps in between.
  • Memoized slices. Risk (_get_returns), Econometrics and Performance cache the return and column slices their methods start from, so collecting many metrics, as the MCP server does in one session, no longer recomputes them for every metric.

Bug Fixes

Risk & Econometrics

  • Whole-series Risk calculations on resampled periods returned NaN, because the first resampled return is always NaN. That row is now dropped before the calculation.
  • get_arch_lm_test(within_period=False) produced no values at all under the old yearly default: four yearly observations can't support a 5-lag ARCH test. With the daily default it now returns real results.
  • Fresh installs now resolve statsmodels 0.15, where the ADF test (get_augmented_dickey_fuller) and the ARCH-LM test (get_arch_lm_test) printed a FutureWarning about an upcoming change to their return format. The toolkit is unaffected by that change until statsmodels 0.16, so these two notices are now silenced. Results are identical on statsmodels 0.14 and 0.15.

API key handling

  • Passing the documentation placeholder api_key="FINANCIAL_MODELING_PREP_KEY" used to reach FinancialModelingPrep and come back as a generic "invalid API key", without saying that the example value was never replaced. It's now reported as a placeholder, with a link to get a key, and treated as no key at all (e.g. the Toolkit falls back to Yahoo Finance). This applies to Toolkit, Portfolio, Discovery, FixedIncome and the MCP server.

MCP Server

  • Fresh installs crashed on startup. mcp 2.x removed mcp.server.fastmcp, which the server imports, and the mcp extra had no upper bound, so pip install financetoolkit[mcp] resolved mcp 2.x and failed immediately. The extra now requires mcp[cli]>=1.27.0,<2.
  • rates → get_treasury_rates returned no data. The server built FixedIncome without the FMP API key, which the Treasury par yield curve needs, and the error was swallowed into "No data available". The key is now passed on, and both the FMP and FRED keys are part of the instance cache key, so instances are never shared between keys.
  • The benchmark could silently be a different security. When a requested ticker was also the benchmark (e.g. tickers="AAPL,SPY" with benchmark_ticker="SPY"), the server replaced the benchmark with the first unused fallback. "Benchmark" was then QQQ (739.77 instead of SPY's 762.63 on 2026-09-30), so every beta, alpha and excess return was measured against the wrong index. The requested benchmark is now kept, matching the library; a fallback is only used when the benchmark is the sole ticker. Either way, the response includes a note explaining where the benchmark's data is.
  • The startup log reported "Registered router group '…' → True tool(s)" instead of a count; it now names the registered group.
  • Daily period is no longer blocked for the risk tool, matching the new default.
  • Per-call timing is logged at debug level, so a slow tool can be diagnosed from the logs alone.

Documentation

  • Every method has its own documentation page. The 76 README links that pointed to an anchor on a module page (docs/ratios#collect_profitability_ratios) now point to that method's dedicated page (docs/ratios/all-profitability-ratios).
  • 21 Econometrics methods, including get_vif, get_ols, the heteroskedasticity and specification tests, the nested-model tests, Fama-MacBeth, synthetic control and the VAR forecast, previously had a single sentence plus a pointer to an internal function the website doesn't show. Each now explains what it computes, the formula, how to read the result for the tickers involved, and the original reference.
  • 31 Econometrics docstrings still said period followed the Toolkit's quarterly/yearly setting; they now document the actual "daily" default.
  • FixedIncome.get_government_bond_yield opened with the 10-year description even when short_term=True returns the 3-month rate. Both maturities are now described, including that the OECD short-term figure is the 3-month interbank rate rather than a Treasury bill yield.
  • get_dual_gamma reused the gamma description; it now describes the second derivative with respect to the strike price.
  • The dead Global Macro Database link in get_gross_domestic_product now points to the GMD documentation page.

Typing

  • The package now ships py.typed, so downstream type checkers see its annotations.
  • uv check (Astral's ty) runs in pre-commit and in the linting workflow. Five rules are back at their default severity (call-non-callable, not-iterable, not-subscriptable, unsupported-operator, unknown-argument), with the code they flagged fixed. 29 stale type: ignore comments are gone. The rules that only reflect pandas' very wide Series | DataFrame return types stay disabled.

Test Coverage & CI

  • Toolkit parameter validation (dates, risk-free rate, source, intraday period, tickers) now lives in its own module, validation_model, so bad input can be tested without building a Toolkit and fetching data.
  • CI runs the suite in parallel (pytest-xdist) with the uv cache. The Economics tests skip cleanly when offline or without a FRED key, instead of erroring.
  • The recorder gains --rewrite-failing, which regenerates only the stored outputs that fail comparison, so a regeneration can't churn unrelated files through float noise.
  • New tests cover the MCP provider (the treasury key and the benchmark handling) and the placeholder API key.
  • A version-alignment test makes sure pyproject.toml, server.json, the MCPB manifest and the MCPB bundle's own pyproject.toml all carry the same version.
  • A Python 3.15 job runs in CI and is skipped until the lock file contains SciPy wheels for 3.15, rather than compiling SciPy from source on the runner.

Dependencies

  • mcp[cli]>=1.27.0,<2 in the mcp extra (see MCP Server above).
  • Lockfile updates: cryptography 50.0.0, httpx2/httpcore2 2.12.0, jupyterlab 4.6.4, notebook 7.6.3, pyjwt 2.15.0, tornado 6.5.9, urllib3 2.8.0.

Full comparison: v2.2.0...v2.2.1

name: FinanceToolkit v2.2.0
html:
This is the largest release to date. The headline addition is a brand new Econometrics module (toolkit.econometrics) — 48 methods covering regression, panel data, causal inference, unit root/cointegration testing, Granger causality, diagnostics, and forecasting, all funneled through statsmodels/linearmodels instead of hand-built math. Alongside it, Risk, Performance, Models and Economics roughly double in depth with systemic-risk, market-timing, bankruptcy-scoring and crisis-dating metrics, and Technicals, Ratios, Fixed Income and Options each pick up a batch of previously-missing metrics.

The second large addition is a rebuilt caching layer. Three separate, incompatible caching mechanisms have been replaced by one incremental, range-aware SQLite cache that knows what it already holds per ticker and per date range — widening a period now retrieves only the missing years, and adding a ticker retrieves only that ticker. It also removes a genuine correctness bug in the old one, which silently overwrote the tickers and dates you asked for with whatever an earlier cached run had used. See Caching below.

Just as importantly, this release includes an extensive formula-correctness pass across nearly every module, carried out over two separate audit rounds — the second explicitly re-checking the first round's own fixes rather than trusting them. Every accepted finding was verified against live FMP/FRED/OECD/ECB/NY Fed data, published figures from BLS/BEA/the US Treasury/Ken French/the source papers, a reference library (TA-Lib/arch/statsmodels/linearmodels/py_vollib) where one exists, or analytic ground truth via Monte Carlo and finite differences. Combined, this fixed over 200 defects. Several of these are not edge-case bugs — Sharpe Ratio, Sortino Ratio, M2 Ratio, RSI, ADX, ATR, EWMA Volatility, the Hurst Exponent, Macaulay's Duration, bond DV01, Portfolio Volatility, US "headline" unemployment and every price-to-fundamental ratio on the LSE/JSE/TASE were all silently returning the wrong number in prior releases. See Bug Fixes below for the full list with what changed and why.

Minimum requirements changed: pandas>=3.0 (was >=2.2) and Python 3.11+ (was 3.10+, since pandas 3.0 itself drops 3.10 support).

Every method below hangs off the matching Toolkit sub-module (e.g. toolkit.econometrics.get_ols()) or its standalone class (Discovery(...), Economics(...), FixedIncome(...)). Full runnable examples with real output live in the documentation — each section below links to its module's page.

New Features

Econometrics (new module)

toolkit.econometrics is a new, optional module for testing statistical properties of price/return series and estimating causal effects — installed via the financetoolkit[econometrics] extra (statsmodels/linearmodels). Every result is a plain dict (matching the rest of the codebase's convention of returning pd.Series/pd.DataFrame rather than opaque result objects), with a matching *_summary_table/*_summary companion wherever a .summary() would otherwise be expected. Full examples: docs/econometrics.

  • Regression: get_ols, get_wls, get_gls (nonrobust/HC0-3/cluster/HAC-Newey-West standard errors), get_logistic_regression, get_probit_regression, get_quantile_regression.
  • Panel data: get_fixed_effects, get_random_effects, get_hausman_test (which specification to prefer).

Risk

Call these via toolkit.risk.<method>(). Full examples: docs/risk.

  • get_covar (CoVaR / Delta-CoVaR) — how much returns' own tail risk worsens when conditioning_returns (e.g. the financial system, or a specific counterparty) is itself in distress, via quantile regression. Reference: Adrian, T. & Brunnermeier, M.K. (2016), American Economic Review.
  • get_marginal_value_at_risk / get_component_value_at_risk — Euler risk decomposition of portfolio VaR: Marginal VaR is each asset's Beta to the portfolio times portfolio VaR; Component VaR is that scaled by the asset's weight, and the components sum exactly to total portfolio VaR (Garman 1997, Litterman 1996).
  • get_amihud_illiquidity (Amihud 2002) and get_roll_spread (Roll 1984) — market-microstructure liquidity measures derived purely from price/volume, without needing order-book data.
  • get_volatility(method=...) — four realized-volatility estimators ("parkinson", "garman_klass", "rogers_satchell", "yang_zhang") built from daily OHLC(V) prices rather than just closes, each using more of the day's price action (and, for Yang-Zhang, overnight gaps) to estimate volatility more efficiently than a close-to-close standard deviation. The default method="close_to_close" is the existing behaviour.
  • get_har_rv_forecast (Corsi 2009 HAR-RV) — forecasts future realized variance from a simple linear combination of daily, weekly and monthly lagged realized variance, a cheap and surprisingly effective alternative to a full GARCH fit.

  • get_gjr_garch / get_egarch (plus _forecast/_parameters variants, and get_garch_parameters for the plain model) — asymmetric GARCH models where negative and positive shocks affect future volatility differently (the leverage effect), unlike plain GARCH. References: Glosten, Jagannathan & Runkle (1993); Nelson (1991).
  • get_var_backtest — builds a rolling, out-of-sample VaR path and backtests it with the Kupiec (1995) proportion-of-failures test and the Christoffersen (1998) independence test, to check whether a VaR model's breach rate and breach clustering match what the confidence level implies.

Caching (rebuilt)

use_cached_data=True still turns caching on, but what happens underneath is entirely new. Where the old cache stored one pickle per dataset and could only ever answer "same request as last time, or nothing", the new one records which tickers and which date ranges it actually holds, and asks the API only for what is missing.

  • Incremental and range-aware. Repeating a request retrieves nothing at all. Widening start_date/end_date retrieves only the years that were not already there. Adding a ticker retrieves only that ticker. Previously any change to any parameter refetched everything.
  • Every external source is covered — financial statements, historical and intraday prices, FRED series, OECD queries, treasury rates, futures contracts, company profiles, quotes, ratings, analyst estimates, earnings and dividend calendars, ESG scores, segmentations, Commitment of Traders, option chains and expiries, GMD, ECB, Fed, Ken French factor datasets, the market risk premium and the discovery endpoints. Anything the Toolkit computes itself is never cached — it is always derived from that data on demand.
  • One shared database. It lives in your platform's user configuration directory (overridable with FINANCE_TOOLKIT_CACHE_DB, or by passing a folder to use_cached_data), which is the same file the MCP server uses, so a local server and the library warm each other's cache instead of each keeping their own.
  • Two freshness knobs per dataset. A time-to-live decides whether to refresh at all, and a revision window decides how much of the recent tail is re-requested when it does — so a rerun inside the TTL makes zero external calls, while a stale daily price series re-requests only its last few days rather than its whole history.
  • toolkit.get_cache_contents() reports what is stored, grouped by source and dataset with entity counts and write times.
  • toolkit.clear_cache(source=, dataset=, ticker=, confirm=) is the only way anything is ever removed. Nothing expires or is evicted on its own, not even when the cache's own internal structure changes between versions — a version mismatch is reported and left alone. An unscoped wipe requires confirm=True. It is deliberately not exposed as an MCP tool.
  • The source names are the same ones enforce_source uses ("FinancialModelingPrep", "YahooFinance", "OECD", "FRED", …), so they mean the same thing in both places.
  • A cache is an optimization and never breaks the caller: a corrupt database, a read-only directory or an unreadable entry disables caching with a warning instead of raising, and every read treats a storage failure as a miss.
  • store() originally spanned three separate connections, so two concurrent writers could both record coverage while the second discarded the first's rows — now a single atomic BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction under WAL, verified across 8 concurrent processes.

Your FMP subscription plan is part of the cache key for the five endpoints whose response length depends on it, so a Free-plan response can never be served to a Premium caller on a shared database. Cached price history is also only ever spliced together when the same provider served both halves, since a ticker that fell back to the other provider carries different split and dividend adjustments.

Existing cached/*.pickle directories are ignored rather than migrated — the new cache simply rebuilds on first use, and the old folder can be deleted by hand.

Breaking Changes

  • Minimum Python is now 3.11 (was 3.10) and minimum pandas is now 3.0 (was 2.2) — pandas 3.0 itself drops Python 3.10 support, so both floors moved together.
  • get_relative_vigor_index no longer accepts a volumes argument. Its old "volume-weighted" formula algebraically reduced to plain up_sum / down_sum regardless of volume (volume canceled out of both sides of the ratio), so the parameter never actually did anything; it's been replaced with a correct, bounded 0-1 ratio and the dead parameter removed.
  • get_short_term_coverage_ratio now takes short_term_debt instead of accounts_receivable/inventory/accounts_payable — see Bug Fixes.
  • use_cached_data=True no longer restores your previous parameters. It used to reload tickers, start_date, end_date and quarterly from a configurations.pickle, which meant a cached run could not be given a different ticker list or period without first clearing the cache. Those arguments are now always taken from what you pass. This was a correctness bug rather than a feature (see Bug Fixes), but it is listed here because the old behaviour of initializing Toolkit(use_cached_data=True) with no arguments at all and getting your previous session back no longer works.
  • Caching is now off by default on a hosted MCP server (MCP_TRANSPORT=sse or streamable-http); a local stdio server is unaffected. Set FINANCE_TOOLKIT_CACHE_ENABLED=true to opt back in.
  • financetoolkit.utilities.cache_model has been removed, along with the MCP server's own SQLiteCache. Both are replaced by financetoolkit.cache. These were internal modules, so this only matters if you imported load_cached_data/save_cached_data directly.
  • Rates and ratios are decimals everywhere now. get_treasury_rates, the FRED rate methods, the whole Global Macro Database family, the output gap and get_commercial_real_estate_prices previously returned percentage points. 4.25% is now 0.0425, not 4.25.
  • Quarterly statement labels shift for companies whose fiscal quarters end in January/April/July/October — both frequencies now apply the same month-rule relabelling the annual path always had, so a company's quarters actually sum to its annual figures (they previously didn't for these companies).   • Unreported statement line items are NaN, not 0 — both whole missing rows and, as of this cycle, individual missing cells within an otherwise-reported row on the Yahoo path, which is common for the oldest year of a multi-year statement.
  • Yahoo-sourced non-USD tickers are now currency-converted, where before they silently weren't (Yahoo published no statistics_yf.csv, so Reported Currency was never available for that path).
